text:
Clara: Quick sync — we need to settle long-term routing/isolation scope for H2 roadmap. Sales surfaced multiple asks: per-tenant routing lanes, regional affinity, SLA tiers, and a simple rollback story. Proposing draft launch criteria and gating metrics so we can prioritize. Thoughts?

Jonathan: +1. We need concrete SLO numbers and measurable gating metrics. Also: what does "isolation" mean here — hard tenant isolation (dedicated pools) vs soft isolation (traffic shaping / eviction)?

Lee: From infra: biggest unknowns are cross-region KV cache behavior and fallback plumbing. If we do per-tenant lanes we must define limits for KV state and eviction policies early.

Olivia: Product note — customers expect self-serve controls to pin regions and roll back model variants without manual ops. That affects the console UX and policy surface.

Mike: Ops perspective: runbook + automatic fallback policy are non-negotiable for enterprise launches. Acceptance test idea: induce region outage and verify failover <30s and error increase <2%.

Tara: Sales: three pilot customers are ready to sign up for a dedicated lane feature, but timeline matters — they want a Q4 pilot. They asked for documented SLA behavior and migration docs.

Clara: Draft launch criteria (short):
```
- Latency p95 <= 200ms for regional traffic under typical load profile
- Failover between regions or capacity tiers < 30s, with error delta <= 2%
- Tenant isolation lanes: soft-eviction + per-tenant routing config; clear upgrade path to dedicated pools
- Canary deploys + automatic rollback on quality regressions (defined by prompt evals)
- Console controls + API for region pinning and rollout config
- Runbooks, SLO dashboards, and chaos test coverage
```
Are these reasonable gating items? Anything missing or infeasible?

Jonathan: We should add perf benchmarks for long-tail sequence lengths (>=4096 tokens) to the gating criteria. Also a KV cache warming/rollback story — stopping a tenant on a new cluster must allow quick warm-up or fallback. Recommend canary at 1% traffic for 48h as an operational constraint.

Lee: Agree. Also call out dependency: routing-DSL project needs to ship an initial API (policy matchers, region affinity weight) — I estimate Q3 for a minimal surface. Need to align on wire format (policy JSON sketch).

Olivia: I'll draft a customer rollout matrix (pilot → beta → GA) mapping customer size/SLAs to configuration options (soft lane vs dedicated). That will help prioritize which controls we expose first.

Mike: I'll take runbooks and SLO dashboards. Need eng-runtime to expose these metrics: per-tenant p50/p95/p99, failover latencies, request reroutes. Who owns telemetry? @Lee?

Lee: Yep, runtime team will add the metrics. We need an events schema for reroute/fallback events. I'll slot a spike for that.

Clara: Action items and owners: @Jonathan perf benches and canary baseline (due 1739995000), @Lee routing-DSL API + telemetry schema (due 1740000000), @Olivia customer rollout matrix + docs (due 1740003000), @Mike runbooks + SLO dashboards (due 1740002000). We'll reconvene next Thursday to lock priorities. :thumbsup:

Tara: I'll coordinate pilot customer expectations and share customer-specific constraints (data residency, latency targets).

deploy-bot: Meeting scheduled: "Routing + Isolation Roadmap — initiative planning" on 2024-07-10 10:00 PT.

Clara: Thanks all — please add any missing risks in this thread. Biggest risk I see: cost delta for dedicated lanes vs. customer willingness to pay. We should quantify that before GA.

Jonathan: Risk noted. I'll include a cost-per-tenant sketch with bench numbers.

Lee: Flagging another risk: cross-region egress limits on some clouds may force different fallback behavior per region. Need legal/product signoff for that.

Olivia: I'll capture costs and legal asks in the rollout doc.

Clara: Perfect. Closing for now — please update your items in the sheet and ping me if blockers pop up.
